title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the problem list closing a typescript on Barsotti–Tate (BT) groups and Dieudonné crystals. It cites 'théorème (VII 10.8.2)', so it is evidently a longer or planned version of the Montréal 1970 lectures. The preceding problem (Pb 4, ending at the top of this page) asks whether something becomes Galois-theoretic over the fraction field L of a complete DVR. Notation: A is a complete DVR of mixed characteristic with perfect residue field k, W = W(k), L = Frac(A).

(i) Remark. The functor in question is not essentially surjective even for A = W(k), k algebraically closed. It sends BT groups over A (up to isogeny) to pairs (Dieudonné module M over k, two-step filtration Fil of M ⊗_W L). Not every filtered Dieudonné module arises.

(ii) Problem 5. Make explicit the natural functor from the essential image (a full subcategory of pairs (M, Fil)) to Galois modules over L, i.e. finite-dimensional Q_p-representations of Gal(L̄/L). This is Grothendieck's 'foncteur mystérieux': the functor that should send the filtered Dieudonné module of G to V_p(G) = T_p(G) ⊗ Q_p without passing through G. He also asks whether it can be defined naturally on all pairs, imposing only rank conditions on the graded pieces. In modern terms this is Fontaine's V_cris(D) = (B_cris ⊗ D)^{φ=1} ∩ Fil^0. The answer to the second question is no: one needs weak admissibility, a Newton-above-Hodge semistability condition on all sub-objects, not just rank conditions. Colmez–Fontaine (2000) proved weakly admissible = admissible. For Hodge–Tate weights in {0,1} this matches BT groups (Breuil, Kisin).

(iii) Problem 6. This is the relative version over a more general base A (as in Pb 4, presumably p-adically complete, with A_0 = A/pA and A_p = A[1/p]). Input: an 'admissible' Dieudonné isocrystal M on A_0 (or on A_0,red), plus a two-step filtration of the evaluation (M_A)_p by locally free modules of the right rank. Possibly further Zariski-open conditions guarantee that the pair comes from a BT isogroup over A. Output: lisse p-adic sheaves ('faisceaux p-adiques constants tordus') on U = Spec(A_p). The functor should recover the functor of Thm VII 10.8.2, i.e. G ↦ V_p(G_U). Modern counterparts: relative p-adic Hodge theory and crystalline local systems (Faltings; Brinon; Scholze's pro-étale theory; Kedlaya–Liu; Tan–Tong). They also include period-domain theory, where the locus of filtrations coming from p-divisible groups is studied (Rapoport–Zink, Hartl).

(iv) A crossed-out heading '4) Question des relations entre cohomologie cristalline et p-adique' and a crossed-out 'Conjecture 7'. The latter starts the general mysterious-functor conjecture for complete DVRs V with perfect residue field: a canonical functor on a suitable full subcategory of pairs (M, Fil^·) toward Galois representations. This is the formulation published in his ICM Nice 1970 talk.
errors: Problem 5's hope that rank conditions on the graded pieces suffice is false. Fontaine's weak admissibility (t_H(D') ≤ t_N(D') for all sub-objects, with equality for D) is required; it is a condition on sub-objects, not just ranks.

Problem 6's guess that the extra conditions are 'ouvertes au sens Zariski' is not right in general. In families, the weakly admissible locus is the complement of a countable union of Zariski-closed subsets (Rapoport–Zink), open only in the analytic (Berkovich/adic) topology. Hartl showed the admissible locus is open in the Berkovich sense and generally strictly smaller than the weakly admissible locus.
Minor: 'Dieudonné module M sur k (i.e. module sur W)' should be read as a W(k)-module with F, V.

ideas.what: Mysterious functor from filtered Dieudonné modules to p-adic Galois representations of L, and whether it extends beyond objects coming from BT groups
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux', Actes ICM Nice 1970; Montréal lecture notes 1974

ideas.what: Relative mysterious functor: filtered (admissible) isocrystals on A/p with locally free Hodge filtration → lisse Q_p-sheaves on Spec(A[1/p]), with open conditions characterizing those from BT groups
ideas.modern_name: Relative p-adic Hodge theory / crystalline local systems; admissible locus in period domains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Faltings (1989), Brinon (2008), Scholze (2013), Kedlaya–Liu; period domains: Rapoport–Zink (1996), Hartl (2008–13)
ideas.where_published: Possibly in the Montréal notes' problem section; unsure

ideas.what: Use of the word 'admissible' (handwritten insertion) for Dieudonné isocrystals that come from BT groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly posed the family/relative version of the mysterious functor over a general base. He conjectured that the condition for a filtered isocrystal family to come from a BT isogroup is an open condition, which anticipates the admissible-locus problem for Rapoport–Zink period domains. The idea is well developed later, but this early relative formulation is rarely attributed to him.
missed.quote: soumis éventuellement à d'autres conditions au sens Zar ouvertes, assurant que le couple envisagé provient d'un isogroupe de BT sur A), vers les faisceaux p-adiques constants tordus sur U=Spec(A_p)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows Grothendieck anticipated relative p-adic Hodge theory and the openness of the admissible locus (true analytically, false Zariski-wise), predating Rapoport–Zink and Hartl.

deep.surprise_reason: Problem 5 is the famous, published mysterious-functor question. Problem 6, a relative version with an open-condition guess for coming from BT groups, is a mildly notable early anticipation of period-domain admissibility and relative p-adic Hodge theory. All of this was later fully developed by others.
